summary: Scrapy is a mature, production-grade web crawling and scraping framework built on Twisted with async/await support (since v2.14). The architecture centers on an ExecutionEngine that coordinates a Scheduler, Downloader (with pluggable handlers for HTTP/HTTPS/S3/FTP), and Scraper (with spider middleware, item pipelines, and signal system). Spiders define async start() methods yielding Requests, with callbacks producing Items or new Requests. The framework provides 200+ settings controlling concurrency, retries, throttling, caching, robots.txt, feed exports (JSON/CSV/XML), and JOBDIR persistence. Verified in code: Twisted reactor with asyncio integration, middleware chains for download/spider/item processing, signal-based extensibility, priority-based scheduler, and comprehensive default middleware stack (retry, redirect, cookies, auth, proxy, compression, cache, stats).

apiSurface: Primary: scrapy crawl <spider> CLI; programmatic: CrawlerProcess(settings).crawl(SpiderClass).start() or AsyncCrawlerProcess(settings).crawl(SpiderClass); await runner.crawl(SpiderClass). Spider API: class MySpider(Spider): name='x'; async def start(self): yield Request(url); async def parse(self, response): yield Item|Request. Settings via Settings dict or settings.py. Middlewares/pipelines/extensions via settings dicts with priority ints. Signals via crawler.signals.connect(handler, signal). Feed exports via FEEDS dict.
integrationPoints: Playwright integration via scrapy-playwright (external package) - download handler replaces HTTP11 for JS-rendered pages. Queue: Scrapy's Scheduler is internal; for distributed crawling use scrapy-redis or scrapy-cluster. Search: not built-in; feed exports can pipe to Elasticsearch/Meilisearch via custom FeedStorage. Matching: item pipelines can implement deduplication/matching logic. For Veridian: use scrapy-playwright for laptop vendor JS sites, feed exports to JSONL for ETL pipeline, custom item pipeline for spec normalization/matching, JOBDIR for resume capability, AutoThrottle for polite scraping.
strengthsForVeridian: Battle-tested at massive scale (Zyte), comprehensive middleware for cross-cutting concerns (retry, throttle, cache, robots), async-first modern API, built-in feed exports to multiple formats/destinations, JOBDIR for crash recovery, extensible via signals/middlewares/pipelines/addons, excellent docs, active maintenance. Deterministic request/response model fits ETL pipelines well.
weaknessesForVeridian: No native JavaScript rendering (requires scrapy-playwright or Splash), Twisted learning curve steep for non-Twisted devs, reactor management complexity, single-process (distributed needs external tools), no built-in browser fingerprinting/evasion, settings sprawl (200+ knobs), synchronous default settings loading can surprise. For laptop specs: vendor sites often need JS rendering; scrapy-playwright adds dependency but works.
